blocks.text:
# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` / `--timer`/`--deadline` / `/timer` write one
  session clock, the per-turn context carries a `time-left:` line while
  armed, and one-shot system notices steer wrap-up at ~50%, T-3min
  (drain background jobs), and T-30s; absent deadline = byte-for-byte
  today's behavior.

- gh-1522: tag-sourced versions — the git tag is the single source of
  truth. The release-bot file bumps are retired: cutting a release = a
  tag + GitHub Release (zero commits to main, zero file mutations).
  Both pubspecs carry the fixed `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (CI guards
  hand-bumps), the publish job stamps the staged pubspec + generated
  changelog section from the tag (`scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`,
  staged version == tag guarded pre-upload), store builds stamp
  `--build-name/--build-number` from the derived tag version
  (`pubspec.lock` stops churning across releases), and
  `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from `git describe`.

- feat(usage): gh-1460 — the `fa-tokens:` segment-close line carries the
  session's model id, so every token row the factory publishes is
  attributable to a model and therefore priceable. The fold now captures
  each segment's LAST-SEEN model id (the model that served the final
  request, the same string settings/UI display — mid-session fallback
  take-overs attribute the segment to the model that actually finished it;
  zero-filled fallbacks never clobber a seen model) and the pinned line
  shape grows an OPTIONAL `"model":"<id>"` key after `"segment"` — omitted
  when no model was observed, so legacy lines parse unchanged and the
  pinned regex (`usageTokensLogPattern`, gh-1241 AC7) keeps matching both
  shapes. usage.json's schema is untouched (the model is rebuildable from
  the chain, I6); old consumers using tolerant JSON ignore the new key,
  and the repo's single strict consumer (the pinned constant) is updated
  in the same change.

- fix(test): gh-1460 rework — the `wrap_ansi_line_perf_test` growth-shape
  legs measure the doubling ratio with the MINIMUM over 9 runs instead of
  the median of 5 (CI run 38112524699, core shard 0/4: a scheduling pause
  inflated the doubled-size median — 12.09ms against a true ~7ms — and
  tripped the 3.2 bound at 3.65x on a genuinely linear wrap). Runner
  jitter only ever inflates a wall-clock sample, so the min converges on
  the true compute time; genuine superlinearity still trips the ratio
  (the gh-1496 quadratic candidates measure ~4x by min). The absolute-
  budget legs keep the median — their gh-1357 headroom already prices in
  jitter. A synthetic regression test pins the pause-proof property.

## 1.0.506

- fix(#1044): AIIN mobile/macOS add-provider — sign-in completes but the provider is never added (#1194)
- fix(ci): pass flutter-version explicitly — awf no longer defaults a toolchain (#1205)

## 1.0.507

- gh-1208 [BENCH] fix-git task image broken on CI runners — docker compose build fails in BOTH TBench-1 runs (unknown_agent_error, trial never starts) (#1218)
- gh-1206 WIP auto-save 2026-10-04T05-52-28 (#1216)
- gh-1209 [BENCH] usage fold skips failed trials — agent_timeout rows report 0/0 tokens though the session JSONL has full usage (#1123 follow-up) (#1215)

## 1.0.508

- fix(cli): gh-1459 — headless `fa -p` no longer orphans live background
  shell jobs. `_awaitHeadlessBackgroundJobs` drained only in-flight
  subagent jobs, so a run whose model was still waiting on a
  `bash background:true` command (gh-1440's full test suite) printed the
  detach summary and exited, killing the job with the container — the
  result it was explicitly waiting for never reached anyone. Live shell
  jobs now drain exactly like subagents: the settles ride the existing
  `_onShellJobSettled` fresh-turn path (steered into reaction runs the
  drain awaits, loop capped at 10 rounds), suppressed jobs
  (`suppressSettleNotification` — result already landed in-turn) are not
  awaited, and a settle landing outside a round still gets its reaction
  run awaited before exit. BOTH loops share ONE wall-clock ceiling, the
  new `headless:` config section (`shellJobDrainMs`, default 30 min,
  strict parse; `0` restores the detach-immediately behavior) — a
  never-settling watch-loop detaches with an observable
  `⏳ … drain ceiling … — detaching` line instead of hanging headless,
  and the detach summary stays the documented degradation, never the
  default path. The drain prints a `⏳ waiting: …` line (#1055 parity)
  naming what the run stays alive for. While it waits, the drain also
  steers interim liveness notices (gh-1459 ask #4): every
  `headless.shellJobQuietMs` (default 5 min; `0` = off) of a
  still-running awaited shell job, ONE compact system-notice
  (`job <id> running · <elapsed> elapsed · tail: …` plus the bash_job
  output/stop escape hatch) keeps the model able to wait, inspect, or
  kill instead of blocking blindly to the ceiling; a crossing the model
  probed itself (`bash_job status/output` bumps the entry's probe
  generation) is skipped, one steer budget per threshold, never a spam
  loop.
- feat(providers): issue #1398 — stall-recovery tuning becomes per-provider
  and data-driven. Registry entries (`customProviders:`, `models.custom:`,
  roles chain entries, `providersQueue:` entries) accept optional
  `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs` (strict positive-int parsing);
  resolution is **entry > the `providerTimeouts:` section > the 180 s/300 s
  defaults**, per field, and every seeded entry prints its effective values

# fa CLI — TUI render/input performance

Status: **in progress** on branch `perf/tui-stream-render`.
Canonical perf log for the fa interactive TUI (`lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart`,
`lib/src/cli/ansi_markdown.dart`), modeled on yoxterm's
[PERFORMANCE.md](../../../../yoloit/yoloit/packages/xterm/docs/PERFORMANCE.md)
and its distilled rules
([PERFORMANCE_BEST_PRACTICES.md](../../../../yoloit/yoloit/packages/xterm/docs/PERFORMANCE_BEST_PRACTICES.md)).

## Goal

Streaming a long answer must never make typing feel dead. Concretely:

- While output streams at the coalesced rate (~20 flushes/s), a keystroke
  must reach the screen within a frame (< ~16 ms of competing work) — not
  behind multi-ms markdown re-parses of the whole history.
- Visual output must stay byte-identical: the integration terminal
  snapshots and `tui_prototype_snapshot_test` are the regression gate.

## The measured baseline (this machine, AOT `dart run`, 2026-08)

Simulation of one coalesced flush over a full history
(`tool/tui_stream_bench.dart --lines 2000 --iters 25`, mixed-content
2000-line transcript — headers/bullets/inline code/links/fenced code/CJK+
emoji/table), i.e. what `_wrappedLines()` pays on EVERY flush because the
markdown pass has no memory between calls:

| Hot path | cost |
|---|---|
| `AnsiMarkdown.formatAll(2000 lines)` + wrap of all rows | **26.96 ms/pass** |
| Share of each 50 ms streaming-flush interval | **53.9%** |
| Full-history passes per streamed answer (≈20/s × minutes) | thousands |

Root cause mapping to the yoxterm rules we violated:

1. **§4 persistent parser state across chunks** — `AnsiMarkdown` is a
   per-call object: `_inFence` + the pending-table buffer die at the end
   of every `formatAll`, so nothing can ever be resumed; the whole
   transcript is re-parsed from line 0 twenty times a second.
2. **§2 damage tracking / version boundaries** — `_WrapCache` memoizes on
   list identity only: an append invalidates ALL rows, even though the
   first 1995 lines did not change. Re-wrapped them all anyway.

(Already shipped earlier and kept: §5 producer throttling — the 50 ms
`sendOutput` coalescing timer.)

## The fix: prefix-committed incremental formatting

A `TranscriptMarkdown` session owned by `_WrapCache`:

- Commits formatted results through an index `_through`, carrying the
  cross-line state (`_inFence`) across calls — the persistent-parser
  rule. Subsequent appends format ONLY the appended suffix.
- A resume boundary is valid only when the pending-table buffer is empty
  AND the raw first line is unchanged (the trim path drops lines from the
  FRONT, which flips the sentinel cheaply). Any violation → today's full
  rebuild path; correctness never depends on the guess.
- Wrap results are cached per committed source line as well (`rows`,
  `lineStartRows` extended in place); unchanged prefixes are neither
  re-formatted nor re-wrapped nor re-indexed.
- Width change or a shorter source ⇒ documented full-rebuild fallback =
  current behavior.

## Contract tests (work counters, not timings — CI-safe)

`test/cli/transcript_markdown_perf_test.dart` asserts, via debug counters
on `TranscriptMarkdown`:

1. Parity: incremental sync steps ≡ one-shot `formatAll` for adversarial
   transcripts (fence spanning a resume boundary, table at the boundary,
   table spanning many syncs, pre-styled echo lines, CJK/emoji, resize
   rebuild, front-trim rebuild).
2. Work counters: N append-syncs after the initial load format only the
   appended lines (sum of formatted lines ≈ total added + boundary look
   ahead), full rebuilds == expected triggers.
3. The model layer keeps its O(delta) property under the exact mutation
   pattern the controller produces during streaming.

## Results

Same machine, AOT `dart run`, simulation of one coalesced flush over the
2000-line mixed transcript (`tool/tui_stream_bench.dart` before,
`tool/tx_after_bench.dart` after):

| path | before | after | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| streaming flush (grow pass, +1 burst) | **26 960 µs** | **37 µs** | **×729** |
| share of each 50 ms flush interval | 53.9 % | **0.07 %** | input no longer queues behind renders |
| keystroke-race sync (cache hit) | n/a (full pass) | **< 1 µs** | O(1) |

Contract gates shipped with it:

- `test/cli/transcript_markdown_perf_test.dart` — parity fixtures
  (fences/tables/pre-styled/CJK+emoji spanning boundaries), byte-exact
  outputs on BOTH resume and documented rebuild paths, work counters
  (`debugLinesFormatted` == delta lines appended, `debugFullRebuilds`
  counts only width changes / head-trims / tail replacements).
- Visual regression: `fa_tui_test`, `tui_prototype_snapshot_test`,
  `ansi_markdown_test` (+110 checks) green unchanged; PTY integration
  snapshots unaffected (formatter is below their layer).

Known boundary (documented, safe): after a front-trim (history cap) or a
tail-regenerating caller the next sync takes ONE legacy full pass —
byte-exact, then resumes incrementally.

## Change log

- branch opened with baseline bench + this doc (no behavior change yet).
- issue #43: the 32KB tail hard-split now resumes instead of rebuilding
  (see the section below).

## Issue #43 — typing during thinking streams: the 32KB tail hard-split

A minutes-long no-newline thinking stream crosses
`fa_tui._appendOutput`'s 32KB tail cap, which re-splits the tail into
16KB chunk lines — fresh substring identities every time. When a split
landed while the commit boundary sat ON the growing tail (the
just-committed phase of the flush cycle), both identity sentinels missed
and that sync took the full O(transcript) rebuild. The cost grows with
the session, so minutes-long thinking degraded typing progressively:
real-PTY e2e at 200 reasoning deltas/s, 60s in (≈1.4MB transcript):
frame-build p99 24.8ms, max 81ms; keystroke echo p99 59.5ms, max 100ms.

Fix (`TranscriptMarkdown._rollbackGrownTail`): the rollback also
recognizes the split shape — the boundary line survives as a prefix of
the concatenated chunks (one O(boundary) string compare per suspected
split, `_boundarySurvivesAsChunks`) — rolls back ONE source line and
re-walks the chunks. Replaced (non-faithful) content still takes the
documented rebuild path.

Measured after: rebuilds in the flood regime 0 across all runs
(before: phase-race, 0–5 per 30s in-process bench); frame-build
p99 5.0ms / max 7.4ms flat over 60s; echo p99 43.6ms, max 57.3ms
(residual tail is event-loop/GC noise from the flood itself, bounded,
not growing with transcript size). Bench:
`dart run scripts/tui_typing_bench.dart --grow-tail` (in-process rebuild
counters; seeds the submit-echo lines so the flood grows the LAST line
like the shipped REPL). Contracts: the split-resume trio in
`test/cli/transcript_markdown_perf_test.dart`.

## Table rendering — adversarial TDD round (post-optimization)

The speedup initially exposed (and testing then pinned) a real streaming-table
correctness bug — the same class as the historical "tables fall apart while a
run streams" reports:

*Root cause.* The durable-commit boundary advanced past a STILL-OPEN table.
The frozen snapshot carries only fence state; buffered table rows live solely
in the parser buffer, so once the boundary crossed them those leading rows
were never re-consumed — later renders lost the header row or shifted cells,
and rebuilds ended pending with unreplayable state.

*Invariant now enforced* (`TranscriptMarkdown._commitTo`):

> The commit edge stops at the last CLEAN step — it NEVER advances into an
> open table span (`through = from + lastClean + 1`). Until the table closes,
> its whole span stays provisional: every flush re-renders exactly that span
> from the frozen state and replaces the previous frame wholesale (no ghosts,
> no stacking), which also keeps late-widening columns safe. Close drains the
> full rendered grid into durable caches exactly once.

Both resume and rebuild paths share one walker (`_walk` → `_commitTo` /
`_expose`), so the invariant cannot drift between them.

Contracts: `test/cli/transcript_table_render_test.dart` — stepped parity at
every prefix (including ending-mid-table), late column widening, CJK/emoji
display widths + border-alignment checks on s…

Actually wait. What about the physical screen-scroll behavior: when the frame grows taller than the terminal (frame rows > termHeight), `_cropToGlass` drops from the top. But BEFORE that guard existed... it exists.

Alternative: the CellRenderer's scroll-region fast path (CSI S/CSI T). Scenario: answer streams in → history grows → the frame's history window slides down (rows shift UP). The renderer detects a shift-up by k, emits `CSI kS` (scroll up), then repaints the k fresh rows at the bottom. If, instead, the content change is NOT a pure shift (e.g. a service row inserted in the live area changes the middle), and detection still picks a k within tolerance... then the "repaint" rows are only the mismatches — but a shift op PHYSICALLY scrolls the screen, pushing the top rows off — in alt screen, top rows are LOST, and the invariant check (static-edge) rejects... The static-edge check rejects when the EDGE row is identical AND non-blank.

Consider: transcript window with sticky chrome at row 0. New frame: history shifted up by k (fresh answer rows at the bottom of the window), sticky echo at row 0 IDENTICAL (the pinned user echo stays). Edge row 0 identical + non-blank → REJECT the scroll op → cell diff. OK.

Detection requires a GLOBAL shift (majority). With a 24-row screen, one removed row shifts ~8 rows up; majority fails → cell diff. OK.

blocks.text:
# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` / `--timer`/`--deadline` / `/timer` write one
  session clock, the per-turn context carries a `time-left:` line while
  armed, and one-shot system notices steer wrap-up at ~50%, T-3min
  (drain background jobs), and T-30s; absent deadline = byte-for-byte
  today's behavior.

- gh-1522: tag-sourced versions — the git tag is the single source of
  truth. The release-bot file bumps are retired: cutting a release = a
  tag + GitHub Release (zero commits to main, zero file mutations).
  Both pubspecs carry the fixed `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (CI guards
  hand-bumps), the publish job stamps the staged pubspec + generated
  changelog section from the tag (`scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`,
  staged version == tag guarded pre-upload), store builds stamp
  `--build-name/--build-number` from the derived tag version
  (`pubspec.lock` stops churning across releases), and
  `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from `git describe`.

- feat(usage): gh-1460 — the `fa-tokens:` segment-close line carries the
  session's model id, so every token row the factory publishes is
  attributable to a model and therefore priceable. The fold now captures
  each segment's LAST-SEEN model id (the model that served the final
  request, the same string settings/UI display — mid-session fallback
  take-overs attribute the segment to the model that actually finished it;
  zero-filled fallbacks never clobber a seen model) and the pinned line
  shape grows an OPTIONAL `"model":"<id>"` key after `"segment"` — omitted
  when no model was observed, so legacy lines parse unchanged and the
  pinned regex (`usageTokensLogPattern`, gh-1241 AC7) keeps matching both
  shapes. usage.json's schema is untouched (the model is rebuildable from
  the chain, I6); old consumers using tolerant JSON ignore the new key,
  and the repo's single strict consumer (the pinned constant) is updated
  in the same change.

- fix(test): gh-1460 rework — the `wrap_ansi_line_perf_test` growth-shape
  legs measure the doubling ratio with the MINIMUM over 9 runs instead of
  the median of 5 (CI run 38112524699, core shard 0/4: a scheduling pause
  inflated the doubled-size median — 12.09ms against a true ~7ms — and
  tripped the 3.2 bound at 3.65x on a genuinely linear wrap). Runner
  jitter only ever inflates a wall-clock sample, so the min converges on
  the true compute time; genuine superlinearity still trips the ratio
  (the gh-1496 quadratic candidates measure ~4x by min). The absolute-
  budget legs keep the median — their gh-1357 headroom already prices in
  jitter. A synthetic regression test pins the pause-proof property.

## 1.0.506

- fix(#1044): AIIN mobile/macOS add-provider — sign-in completes but the provider is never added (#1194)
- fix(ci): pass flutter-version explicitly — awf no longer defaults a toolchain (#1205)

## 1.0.507

- gh-1208 [BENCH] fix-git task image broken on CI runners — docker compose build fails in BOTH TBench-1 runs (unknown_agent_error, trial never starts) (#1218)
- gh-1206 WIP auto-save 2026-10-04T05-52-28 (#1216)
- gh-1209 [BENCH] usage fold skips failed trials — agent_timeout rows report 0/0 tokens though the session JSONL has full usage (#1123 follow-up) (#1215)

## 1.0.508

- fix(cli): gh-1459 — headless `fa -p` no longer orphans live background
  shell jobs. `_awaitHeadlessBackgroundJobs` drained only in-flight
  subagent jobs, so a run whose model was still waiting on a
  `bash background:true` command (gh-1440's full test suite) printed the
  detach summary and exited, killing the job with the container — the
  result it was explicitly waiting for never reached anyone. Live shell
  jobs now drain exactly like subagents: the settles ride the existing
  `_onShellJobSettled` fresh-turn path (steered into reaction runs the
  drain awaits, loop capped at 10 rounds), suppressed jobs
  (`suppressSettleNotification` — result already landed in-turn) are not
  awaited, and a settle landing outside a round still gets its reaction
  run awaited before exit. BOTH loops share ONE wall-clock ceiling, the
  new `headless:` config section (`shellJobDrainMs`, default 30 min,
  strict parse; `0` restores the detach-immediately behavior) — a
  never-settling watch-loop detaches with an observable
  `⏳ … drain ceiling … — detaching` line instead of hanging headless,
  and the detach summary stays the documented degradation, never the
  default path. The drain prints a `⏳ waiting: …` line (#1055 parity)
  naming what the run stays alive for. While it waits, the drain also
  steers interim liveness notices (gh-1459 ask #4): every
  `headless.shellJobQuietMs` (default 5 min; `0` = off) of a
  still-running awaited shell job, ONE compact system-notice
  (`job <id> running · <elapsed> elapsed · tail: …` plus the bash_job
  output/stop escape hatch) keeps the model able to wait, inspect, or
  kill instead of blocking blindly to the ceiling; a crossing the model
  probed itself (`bash_job status/output` bumps the entry's probe
  generation) is skipped, one steer budget per threshold, never a spam
  loop.
- feat(providers): issue #1398 — stall-recovery tuning becomes per-provider
  and data-driven. Registry entries (`customProviders:`, `models.custom:`,
  roles chain entries, `providersQueue:` entries) accept optional
  `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs` (strict positive-int parsing);
  resolution is **entry > the `providerTimeouts:` section > the 180 s/300 s
  defaults**, per field, and every seeded entry prints its effective values

Let me now write a quick reproduction attempt mentally and then actually examine the transcript sync logic for the "service line inserted" scenario.

The claim: "transcript commit offset (O(delta)) re-emitting already-committed lines when a service line (job settle, btw) is inserted between the live area and the previous commit."

Scenario in outputLines terms:
1. Answer streams: lines appended. Last line grows without newline. Commits track it.
2. A `[btw]` notice arrives → `sendOutput('[btw] ...', newline: true)` — appends '\n'... wait, actually the host appends text WITH newline. Let me check the exact append shape: `_appendOutput(lines, text, newline)`: splits text on '\n', merges first part into last line, adds the rest, and if newline=true adds ANOTHER empty line.

Actually wait — for the streaming answer, deltas arrive via `io.write(delta)` → `sendOutput(delta)` with newline=false. The trailing `io.write('\n')` at message end → sendOutput('\n') → parts = ['',''], first part merges ('' into last line), then adds '' → i.e. terminates the last line and opens a new empty line.

So during streaming, outputLines ends with a growing line. `_through` == src.length after each sync (committing the growing tail line!). Then next delta: src[_through-1] is a NEW longer string with the same prefix → `_rollbackGrownTail` rolls back one line and re-walks. Fine.

NOW: a service line (btw notice) lands BETWEEN answer deltas? The ticket: "Happens after a background bash job settles (row like sh-3-...) and [btw] notices about mail/scheduler." The btw notices and job-settle service lines arrive WHILE THE ANSWER IS STREAMING (the answer is the last thing; the notices arrive mid-stream or right at the end).

Order of events for the observed bug:
1. The final answer streams into the transcript (with a table inside → table layout).
2. Meanwhile, service lines (btw) get appended — they go AFTER the growing answer line (outputLines append). That's fine.
3. ...

Hmm, but where would "re-emitting already-committed lines" produce VISIBLE duplication? If TranscriptMarkdown served a stale view (e.g. published `_viewRows` built from OLD `_rows` + new tail WITHOUT the truncation), you'd get duplicated rows!

LOOK at `_expose` closely:

```dart
void _expose(_WalkResult r, List<String> src) {
  final tailStartStep = r.lastClean + 1;
  final tailLines = <String>[
    for (var step = tailStartStep; step < r.outsPerLine.length; step++)
      ...r.outsPerLine[step],
    ...r.trailing,
  ];
  if (tailLines.isEmpty) {
    _publishCleanViews();
    return;
  }
  ...
}
```

`tailLines` = outputs of steps AFTER the commit edge + trailing flush. This looks right.

And in `sync()`:

```dart
final r = _walk(src, from: _through);
_commitTo(r, src, from: _through);
_expose(r, src);
```

_commitTo appends `r.outsPerLine[step]` for step < upto where upto = lastClean+1. So committed steps [0, lastClean], tail steps (lastClean, ...). No overlap. OK.

BUT WAIT — `_rollbackGrownTail`: it rolls back ONE source line (`edge = _through - 1`) and truncates caches. Then `sync` continues:

```dart

if (src.length == _through) { return _viewFormatted; }  // nothing new
...
if (_tailThrottled(src)) { debugTailThrottled++; return _viewFormatted; }
...
final r = _walk(src, from: _through);
_commitTo(r, src, from: _through);
_expose(r, src);
```

After a successful rollback: _through = edge = old _through - 1. src.length is >= _through. If src.length == _through (rollback of the last line but no new lines?) — e.g. the line SHRANK? No: faithful growth means longer.

Hmm OK. Now the table case! The commit edge NEVER advances into an open table span. Consider the answer contains a TABLE (markdown table), and the table is OPEN at the end of the streamed-so-far content (the last rows of the table have arrived but the table hasn't been closed by a blank line / non-table line yet). Then `lastClean` points BEFORE the table start; `upto` stops there. The WHOLE TABLE SPAN is provisional: on every flush it's re-walked from `from = _through` — i.e. `_walk(src, from: _through)` where _through is before the table lines; the walk RE-consumes all the table lines and re-renders them. `_expose` then publishes `_viewRows = [..._rows, ...tailRows]` — a fresh copy with the provisional tail. Still no duplication: `_rows` (durable) has nothing after the boundary.

Hmm, so where's the bug?!

Let me look at the case where `lastClean == -1` and `upto <= 0` → `_commitTo` returns early without doing anything. Then `_expose` with tailStartStep = 0 → tailLines = ALL steps' outputs + trailing. Views = _rows (durable, up to boundary) + tail. Still fine.

What if this is about the **frame diff** in the CELL renderer: rows are only repainted when changed. If the frame content JUMPS (e.g. transcript window content changed completely due to a full rebuild serving DIFFERENT rows), the diff repaints each changed row IN PLACE. If the model produced a frame where the same answer is painted in the history window AND ALSO duplicated rows exist in outputLines... the "two layouts" strongly suggest TWO COPIES of the answer in the FRAME CONTENT itself: one formatted as a table, one raw/glued.

"Lines glued together" — `...гарде2. Issue ...` — this looks like two lines WITHOUT the newline: "гарде" + "2. Issue". When would newlines be lost? If the answer text was re-emitted via a path that STRIPS newlines... e.g. writing text via `io.write` where '\n' separators were replaced...

1. Table layout: the answer WITH structure (markdown source lines, table parsed).
2. Flowing glued text: the same answer content re-appended as ONE LONG LINE (newlines lost!).

Where would the answer get re-emitted with newlines lost?? `io.write(delta)` — deltas... `io.write(text)` where text = the FULL message...

# fa CLI — TUI render/input performance

Status: **in progress** on branch `perf/tui-stream-render`.
Canonical perf log for the fa interactive TUI (`lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart`,
`lib/src/cli/ansi_markdown.dart`), modeled on yoxterm's
[PERFORMANCE.md](../../../../yoloit/yoloit/packages/xterm/docs/PERFORMANCE.md)
and its distilled rules
([PERFORMANCE_BEST_PRACTICES.md](../../../../yoloit/yoloit/packages/xterm/docs/PERFORMANCE_BEST_PRACTICES.md)).

## Goal

Streaming a long answer must never make typing feel dead. Concretely:

- While output streams at the coalesced rate (~20 flushes/s), a keystroke
  must reach the screen within a frame (< ~16 ms of competing work) — not
  behind multi-ms markdown re-parses of the whole history.
- Visual output must stay byte-identical: the integration terminal
  snapshots and `tui_prototype_snapshot_test` are the regression gate.

## The measured baseline (this machine, AOT `dart run`, 2026-08)

Simulation of one coalesced flush over a full history
(`tool/tui_stream_bench.dart --lines 2000 --iters 25`, mixed-content
2000-line transcript — headers/bullets/inline code/links/fenced code/CJK+
emoji/table), i.e. what `_wrappedLines()` pays on EVERY flush because the
markdown pass has no memory between calls:

| Hot path | cost |
|---|---|
| `AnsiMarkdown.formatAll(2000 lines)` + wrap of all rows | **26.96 ms/pass** |
| Share of each 50 ms streaming-flush interval | **53.9%** |
| Full-history passes per streamed answer (≈20/s × minutes) | thousands |

Root cause mapping to the yoxterm rules we violated:

1. **§4 persistent parser state across chunks** — `AnsiMarkdown` is a
   per-call object: `_inFence` + the pending-table buffer die at the end
   of every `formatAll`, so nothing can ever be resumed; the whole
   transcript is re-parsed from line 0 twenty times a second.
2. **§2 damage tracking / version boundaries** — `_WrapCache` memoizes on
   list identity only: an append invalidates ALL rows, even though the
   first 1995 lines did not change. Re-wrapped them all anyway.

(Already shipped earlier and kept: §5 producer throttling — the 50 ms
`sendOutput` coalescing timer.)

## The fix: prefix-committed incremental formatting

A `TranscriptMarkdown` session owned by `_WrapCache`:

- Commits formatted results through an index `_through`, carrying the
  cross-line state (`_inFence`) across calls — the persistent-parser
  rule. Subsequent appends format ONLY the appended suffix.
- A resume boundary is valid only when the pending-table buffer is empty
  AND the raw first line is unchanged (the trim path drops lines from the

## Issue #43 — typing during thinking streams: the 32KB tail hard-split

A minutes-long no-newline thinking stream crosses
`fa_tui._appendOutput`'s 32KB tail cap, which re-splits the tail into
16KB chunk lines — fresh substring identities every time. When a split
landed while the commit boundary sat ON the growing tail (the
just-committed phase of the flush cycle), both identity sentinels missed
and that sync took the full O(transcript) rebuild. The cost grows with
the session, so minutes-long thinking degraded typing progressively:
real-PTY e2e at 200 reasoning deltas/s, 60s in (≈1.4MB transcript):
frame-build p99 24.8ms, max 81ms; keystroke echo p99 59.5ms, max 100ms.

Fix (`TranscriptMarkdown._rollbackGrownTail`): the rollback also
recognizes the split shape — the boundary line survives as a prefix of
the concatenated chunks (one O(boundary) string compare per suspected
split, `_boundarySurvivesAsChunks`) — rolls back ONE source line and
re-walks the chunks. Replaced (non-faithful) content still takes the
documented rebuild path.

Measured after: rebuilds in the flood regime 0 across all runs
(before: phase-race, 0–5 per 30s in-process bench); frame-build
p99 5.0ms / max 7.4ms flat over 60s; echo p99 43.6ms, max 57.3ms
(residual tail is event-loop/GC noise from the flood itself, bounded,
not growing with transcript size). Bench:
`dart run scripts/tui_typing_bench.dart --grow-tail` (in-process rebuild
counters; seeds the submit-echo lines so the flood grows the LAST line
like the shipped REPL). Contracts: the split-resume trio in
`test/cli/transcript_markdown_perf_test.dart`.

correctness bug — the same class as the historical "tables fall apart while a
run streams" reports:

*Root cause.* The durable-commit boundary advanced past a STILL-OPEN table.
The frozen snapshot carries only fence state; buffered table rows live solely
in the parser buffer, so once the boundary crossed them those leading rows
were never re-consumed — later renders lost the header row or shifted cells,
and rebuilds ended pending with unreplayable state.

> The commit edge stops at the last CLEAN step — it NEVER advances into an

> from the frozen state and replaces the previous frame wholesale (no ghosts,
> no stacking), which also keeps late-widening columns safe. Close drains the
> full rendered grid into durable caches exactly once.

Both resume and rebuild paths share one walker (`_walk` → `_commitTo` /
`_expose`), so the invariant cannot drift between them.

# Changelog

on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose

bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the

  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` / `--timer`/`--deadline` / `/timer` write one
  session clock, the per-turn context carries a `time-left:` line while
  armed, and one-shot system notices steer wrap-up at ~50%, T-3min
  (drain background jobs), and T-30s; absent deadline = byte-for-byte
  today's behavior.

- gh-1522: tag-sourced versions — the git tag is the single source of
  truth. The release-bot file bumps are retired: cutting a release = a

  `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from `git describe`.

- feat(usage): gh-1460 — the `fa-tokens:` segment-close line carries the
  session's model id, so every token row the factory publishes is
  attributable to a model and therefore priceable. The fold now captures
  each segment's LAST-SEEN model id (the model that served the final
  request, the same string settings/UI display — mid-session fallback
  take-overs attribute the segment to the model that actually finished it;
  zero-filled fallbacks never clobber a seen model) and the pinned line
  shape grows an OPTIONAL `"model":"<id>"` key after `"segment"` — omitted
  when no model was observed, so legacy lines parse unchanged and the
  pinned regex (`usageTokensLogPattern`, gh-1241 AC7) keeps matching both
  shapes. usage.json's schema is untouched (the model is rebuildable from
  the chain, I6); old consumers using tolerant JSON ignore the new key,
  and the repo's single strict consumer (the pinned constant) is updated
  in the same change.

- fix(test): gh-1460 rework — the `wrap_ansi_line_perf_test` growth-shape
  legs measure the doubling ratio with the MINIMUM over 9 runs instead of
  the median of 5 (CI run 38112524699, core shard 0/4: a scheduling pause
  inflated the doubled-size median — 12.09ms against a true ~7ms — and
  tripped the 3.2 bound at 3.65x on a genuinely linear wrap). Runner

blocks.text:
# fa CLI — TUI render/input performance

Status: **in progress** on branch `perf/tui-stream-render`.
Canonical perf log for the fa interactive TUI (`lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart`,
`lib/src/cli/ansi_markdown.dart`), modeled on yoxterm's
[PERFORMANCE.md](../../../../yoloit/yoloit/packages/xterm/docs/PERFORMANCE.md)
and its distilled rules
([PERFORMANCE_BEST_PRACTICES.md](../../../../yoloit/yoloit/packages/xterm/docs/PERFORMANCE_BEST_PRACTICES.md)).

## Goal

Streaming a long answer must never make typing feel dead. Concretely:

- While output streams at the coalesced rate (~20 flushes/s), a keystroke
  must reach the screen within a frame (< ~16 ms of competing work) — not
  behind multi-ms markdown re-parses of the whole history.
- Visual output must stay byte-identical: the integration terminal
  snapshots and `tui_prototype_snapshot_test` are the regression gate.

## The measured baseline (this machine, AOT `dart run`, 2026-08)

Simulation of one coalesced flush over a full history
(`tool/tui_stream_bench.dart --lines 2000 --iters 25`, mixed-content
2000-line transcript — headers/bullets/inline code/links/fenced code/CJK+
emoji/table), i.e. what `_wrappedLines()` pays on EVERY flush because the
markdown pass has no memory between calls:

| Hot path | cost |
|---|---|
| `AnsiMarkdown.formatAll(2000 lines)` + wrap of all rows | **26.96 ms/pass** |
| Share of each 50 ms streaming-flush interval | **53.9%** |
| Full-history passes per streamed answer (≈20/s × minutes) | thousands |

Root cause mapping to the yoxterm rules we violated:

1. **§4 persistent parser state across chunks** — `AnsiMarkdown` is a
   per-call object: `_inFence` + the pending-table buffer die at the end
   of every `formatAll`, so nothing can ever be resumed; the whole
   transcript is re-parsed from line 0 twenty times a second.
2. **§2 damage tracking / version boundaries** — `_WrapCache` memoizes on
   list identity only: an append invalidates ALL rows, even though the
   first 1995 lines did not change. Re-wrapped them all anyway.

(Already shipped earlier and kept: §5 producer throttling — the 50 ms
`sendOutput` coalescing timer.)

## The fix: prefix-committed incremental formatting

A `TranscriptMarkdown` session owned by `_WrapCache`:

- Commits formatted results through an index `_through`, carrying the
  cross-line state (`_inFence`) across calls — the persistent-parser
  rule. Subsequent appends format ONLY the appended suffix.
- A resume boundary is valid only when the pending-table buffer is empty
  AND the raw first line is unchanged (the trim path drops lines from the
  FRONT, which flips the sentinel cheaply). Any violation → today's full
  rebuild path; correctness never depends on the guess.
- Wrap results are cached per committed source line as well (`rows`,
  `lineStartRows` extended in place); unchanged prefixes are neither
  re-formatted nor re-wrapped nor re-indexed.
- Width change or a shorter source ⇒ documented full-rebuild fallback =
  current behavior.

## Contract tests (work counters, not timings — CI-safe)

`test/cli/transcript_markdown_perf_test.dart` asserts, via debug counters
on `TranscriptMarkdown`:

1. Parity: incremental sync steps ≡ one-shot `formatAll` for adversarial
   transcripts (fence spanning a resume boundary, table at the boundary,
   table spanning many syncs, pre-styled echo lines, CJK/emoji, resize
   rebuild, front-trim rebuild).
2. Work counters: N append-syncs after the initial load format only the
   appended lines (sum of formatted lines ≈ total added + boundary look
   ahead), full rebuilds == expected triggers.
3. The model layer keeps its O(delta) property under the exact mutation
   pattern the controller produces during streaming.

## Results

Same machine, AOT `dart run`, simulation of one coalesced flush over the
2000-line mixed transcript (`tool/tui_stream_bench.dart` before,
`tool/tx_after_bench.dart` after):

| path | before | after | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| streaming flush (grow pass, +1 burst) | **26 960 µs** | **37 µs** | **×729** |
| share of each 50 ms flush interval | 53.9 % | **0.07 %** | input no longer queues behind renders |
| keystroke-race sync (cache hit) | n/a (full pass) | **< 1 µs** | O(1) |

Contract gates shipped with it:

- `test/cli/transcript_markdown_perf_test.dart` — parity fixtures
  (fences/tables/pre-styled/CJK+emoji spanning boundaries), byte-exact
  outputs on BOTH resume and documented rebuild paths, work counters
  (`debugLinesFormatted` == delta lines appended, `debugFullRebuilds`
  counts only width changes / head-trims / tail replacements).
- Visual regression: `fa_tui_test`, `tui_prototype_snapshot_test`,
  `ansi_markdown_test` (+110 checks) green unchanged; PTY integration
  snapshots unaffected (formatter is below their layer).

Known boundary (documented, safe): after a front-trim (history cap) or a
tail-regenerating caller the next sync takes ONE legacy full pass —
byte-exact, then resumes incrementally.

## Change log

- branch opened with baseline bench + this doc (no behavior change yet).
- issue #43: the 32KB tail hard-split now resumes instead of rebuilding
  (see the section below).

## Issue #43 — typing during thinking streams: the 32KB tail hard-split

A minutes-long no-newline thinking stream crosses
`fa_tui._appendOutput`'s 32KB tail cap, which re-splits the tail into
16KB chunk lines — fresh substring identities every time. When a split
landed while the commit boundary sat ON the growing tail (the
just-committed phase of the flush cycle), both identity sentinels missed
and that sync took the full O(transcript) rebuild. The cost grows with
the session, so minutes-long thinking degraded typing progressively:
real-PTY e2e at 200 reasoning deltas/s, 60s in (≈1.4MB transcript):
frame-build p99 24.8ms, max 81ms; keystroke echo p99 59.5ms, max 100ms.

Fix (`TranscriptMarkdown._rollbackGrownTail`): the rollback also
recognizes the split shape — the boundary line survives as a prefix of
the concatenated chunks (one O(boundary) string compare per suspected
split, `_boundarySurvivesAsChunks`) — rolls back ONE source line and
re-walks the chunks. Replaced (non-faithful) content still takes the
documented rebuild path.

Measured after: rebuilds in the flood regime 0 across all runs
(before: phase-race, 0–5 per 30s in-process bench); frame-build
p99 5.0ms / max 7.4ms flat over 60s; echo p99 43.6ms, max 57.3ms
(residual tail is event-loop/GC noise from the flood itself, bounded,
not growing with transcript size). Bench:
`dart run scripts/tui_typing_bench.dart --grow-tail` (in-process rebuild
counters; seeds the submit-echo lines so the flood grows the LAST line
like the shipped REPL). Contracts: the split-resume trio in
`test/cli/transcript_markdown_perf_test.dart`.

## Table rendering — adversarial TDD round (post-optimization)

The speedup initially exposed (and testing then pinned) a real streaming-table
correctness bug — the same class as the historical "tables fall apart while a
run streams" reports:

*Root cause.* The durable-commit boundary advanced past a STILL-OPEN table.
The frozen snapshot carries only fence state; buffered table rows live solely
in the parser buffer, so once the boundary crossed them those leading rows
were never re-consumed — later renders lost the header row or shifted cells,
and rebuilds ended pending with unreplayable state.

*Invariant now enforced* (`TranscriptMarkdown._commitTo`):

> The commit edge stops at the last CLEAN step — it NEVER advances into an
> open table span (`through = from + lastClean + 1`). Until the table closes,
> its whole span stays provisional: every flush re-renders exactly that span
> from the frozen state and replaces the previous frame wholesale (no ghosts,
> no stacking), which also keeps late-widening columns safe. Close drains the
> full rendered grid into durable caches exactly once.

Both resume and rebuild paths share one walker (`_walk` → `_commitTo` /
`_expose`), so the invariant cannot drift between them.

Contracts: `test/cli/transcript_table_render_test.dart` — stepped parity at
every prefix (including ending-mid-table), late column widening, CJK/emoji
display widths + border-alignment checks on s…

This is very useful context. The doc says the table rendering invariant is enforced by `_commitTo` — commit edge stops at the last clean step.

Now — the ticket says the answer rendered 3-4 times "first as a table, then as flowing text with lines glued together". Let me look at `_expose`:
{"limit":160,"offset":1327,"path":"lib/src/cli/ansi_markdown.dart"}

Now — let me look at `_walk` closely. There's an important subtlety in `_walk`:

```dart
_WalkResult _walk(List<String> src, {required int from}) {
  _fmt.restoreState(inFence: _savedFence, table: const []);
  ...
}
```

Hmm, `_fmt.restoreState(inFence: _savedFence, table: const [])` — the table is restored as EMPTY, but the commit edge never advances into an open table span, so the pending table at the boundary should be empty. OK.

Now — the exposure: `_expose` builds `tailLines` from steps AFTER the last clean step. In a resumed sync where all lines were committed cleanly (no open table), `tailStartStep = r.lastClean + 1 = outsPerLine.length`, so `tailLines` = trailing only (usually empty) → `_publishCleanViews()`.

OK so where could duplication come from?

Wait. Let me reconsider. Let me now look at the **`_WrapCache` invalidation contract** — `cache.source` is compared by IDENTITY: `identical(cache.source, outputLines)`. If outputLines identity changed but content is the same... `_wrappedLines` calls `tx.sync(outputLines)` — TranscriptMarkdown handles front-drop via `_boundaryFirst` identity check, etc. And a full rebuild is byte-exact. So the wrap cache level seems robust.

Let me now think about "the answer re-written over the live area ... first as a table, then as flowing text with lines glued together" differently:

Maybe THE ANSWER IS RENDERED IN THE TRANSCRIPT *AND* THE STICKY ECHO + ANOTHER STICKY. What sticks at the top while busy: the USER message (stickyLines). What about... hmm.

"[btw] notices about mail/scheduler" — service lines appended into the transcript. "The answer is re-written over the live area in two layouts".

1. First as markdown source lines → rendered as a table layout (the answer contained a table).
2. Then re-appended raw → rendered as flowing text with glued lines.

And where would the re-append come from? Look at `_onTextDelta` for TUI: `io.write(_redactRendered(delta))`. `io` here is the CliIO. In TUI mode `io.write` routes through `_TuiCliIO.write` → `tui.sendOutput(text)`.

blocks.text:
# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` / `--timer`/`--deadline` / `/timer` write one
  session clock, the per-turn context carries a `time-left:` line while
  armed, and one-shot system notices steer wrap-up at ~50%, T-3min
  (drain background jobs), and T-30s; absent deadline = byte-for-byte
  today's behavior.

- gh-1522: tag-sourced versions — the git tag is the single source of
  truth. The release-bot file bumps are retired: cutting a release = a
  tag + GitHub Release (zero commits to main, zero file mutations).
  Both pubspecs carry the fixed `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (CI guards
  hand-bumps), the publish job stamps the staged pubspec + generated
  changelog section from the tag (`scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`,
  staged version == tag guarded pre-upload), store builds stamp
  `--build-name/--build-number` from the derived tag version
  (`pubspec.lock` stops churning across releases), and
  `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from `git describe`.

- feat(usage): gh-1460 — the `fa-tokens:` segment-close line carries the
  session's model id, so every token row the factory publishes is
  attributable to a model and therefore priceable. The fold now captures
  each segment's LAST-SEEN model id (the model that served the final
  request, the same string settings/UI display — mid-session fallback
  take-overs attribute the segment to the model that actually finished it;
  zero-filled fallbacks never clobber a seen model) and the pinned line
  shape grows an OPTIONAL `"model":"<id>"` key after `"segment"` — omitted
  when no model was observed, so legacy lines parse unchanged and the

# fa CLI — TUI render/input performance

Status: **in progress** on branch `perf/tui-stream-render`.
Canonical perf log for the fa interactive TUI (`lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart`,
`lib/src/cli/ansi_markdown.dart`), modeled on yoxterm's
[PERFORMANCE.md](../../../../yoloit/yoloit/packages/xterm/docs/PERFORMANCE.md)
and its distilled rules
([PERFORMANCE_BEST_PRACTICES.md](../../../../yoloit/yoloit/packages/xterm/docs/PERFORMANCE_BEST_PRACTICES.md)).

## Goal

Streaming a long answer must never make typing feel dead. Concretely:

- While output streams at the coalesced rate (~20 flushes/s), a keystroke
  must reach the screen within a frame (< ~16 ms of competing work) — not
  behind multi-ms markdown re-parses of the whole history.
- Visual output must stay byte-identical: the integration terminal
  snapshots and `tui_prototype_snapshot_test` are the regression gate.

## The measured baseline (this machine, AOT `dart run`, 2026-08)

Simulation of one coalesced flush over a full history
(`tool/tui_stream_bench.dart --lines 2000 --iters 25`, mixed-content
2000-line transcript — headers/bullets/inline code/links/fenced code/CJK+
emoji/table), i.e. what `_wrappedLines()` pays on EVERY flush because the
markdown pass has no memory between calls:

| Hot path | cost |
|---|---|
| `AnsiMarkdown.formatAll(2000 lines)` + wrap of all rows | **26.96 ms/pass** |
| Share of each 50 ms streaming-flush interval | **53.9%** |
| Full-history passes per streamed answer (≈20/s × minutes) | thousands |

Root cause mapping to the yoxterm rules we violated:

1. **§4 persistent parser state across chunks** — `AnsiMarkdown` is a
   per-call object: `_inFence` + the pending-table buffer die at the end
   of every `formatAll`, so nothing can ever be resumed; the whole
   transcript is re-parsed from line 0 twenty times a second.
2. **§2 damage tracking / version boundaries** — `_WrapCache` memoizes on
   list identity only: an append invalidates ALL rows, even though the
   first 1995 lines did not change. Re-wrapped them all anyway.

(Already shipped earlier and kept: §5 producer throttling — the 50 ms
`sendOutput` coalescing timer.)

## The fix: prefix-committed incremental formatting

A `TranscriptMarkdown` session owned by `_WrapCache`:

- Commits formatted results through an index `_through`, carrying the
  cross-line state (`_inFence`) across calls — the persistent-parser
  rule. Subsequent appends format ONLY the appended suffix.
- A resume boundary is valid only when the pending-table buffer is empty
  AND the raw first line is unchanged (the trim path drops lines from the
  FRONT, which flips the sentinel cheaply). Any violation → today's full
  rebuild path; correctness never depends on the guess.
- Wrap results are cached per committed source line as well (`rows`,
  `lineStartRows` extended in place); unchanged prefixes are neither
  re-formatted nor re-wrapped nor re-indexed.
- Width change or a shorter source ⇒ documented full-rebuild fallback =
  current behavior.

## Contract tests (work counters, not timings — CI-safe)

`test/cli/transcript_markdown_perf_test.dart` asserts, via debug counters
on `TranscriptMarkdown`:

1. Parity: incremental sync steps ≡ one-shot `formatAll` for adversarial
   transcripts (fence spanning a resume boundary, table at the boundary,
   table spanning many syncs, pre-styled echo lines, CJK/emoji, resize
   rebuild, front-trim rebuild).
2. Work counters: N append-syncs after the initial load format only the
   appended lines (sum of formatted lines ≈ total added + boundary look
   ahead), full rebuilds == expected triggers.
3. The model layer keeps its O(delta) property under the exact mutation
   pattern the controller produces during streaming.

## Results

Same machine, AOT `dart run`, simulation of one coalesced flush over the
2000-line mixed transcript (`tool/tui_stream_bench.dart` before,
`tool/tx_after_bench.dart` after):

| path | before | after | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| streaming flush (grow pass, +1 burst) | **26 960 µs** | **37 µs** | **×729** |
| share of each 50 ms flush interval | 53.9 % | **0.07 %** | input no longer queues behind renders |
| keystroke-race sync (cache hit) | n/a (full pass) | **< 1 µs** | O(1) |

Contract gates shipped with it:

- `test/cli/transcript_markdown_perf_test.dart` — parity fixtures
  (fences/tables/pre-styled/CJK+emoji spanning boundaries), byte-exact
  outputs on BOTH resume and documented rebuild paths, work counters
  (`debugLinesFormatted` == delta lines appended, `debugFullRebuilds`
  counts only width changes / head-trims / tail replacements).
- Visual regression: `fa_tui_test`, `tui_prototype_snapshot_test`,
  `ansi_markdown_test` (+110 checks) green unchanged; PTY integration
  snapshots unaffected (formatter is below their layer).

Known boundary (documented, safe): after a front-trim (history cap) or a
tail-regenerating caller the next sync takes ONE legacy full pass —
byte-exact, then resumes incrementally.

## Change log

- branch opened with baseline bench + this doc (no behavior change yet).
- issue #43: the 32KB tail hard-split now resumes instead of rebuilding
  (see the section below).

## Issue #43 — typing during thinking streams: the 32KB tail hard-split

A minutes-long no-newline thinking stream crosses
`fa_tui._appendOutput`'s 32KB tail cap, which re-splits the tail into
16KB chunk lines — fresh substring identities every time. When a split
landed while the commit boundary sat ON the growing tail (the
just-committed phase of the flush cycle), both identity sentinels missed
and that sync took the full O(transcript) rebuild. The cost grows with
the session, so minutes-long thinking degraded typing progressively:
real-PTY e2e at 200 reasoning deltas/s, 60s in (≈1.4MB transcript):
frame-build p99 24.8ms, max 81ms; keystroke echo p99 59.5ms, max 100ms.

Fix (`TranscriptMarkdown._rollbackGrownTail`): the rollback also
recognizes the split shape — the boundary line survives as a prefix of
the concatenated chunks (one O(boundary) string compare per suspected
split, `_boundarySurvivesAsChunks`) — rolls back ONE source line and
re-walks the chunks. Replaced (non-faithful) content still takes the
documented rebuild path.

Measured after: rebuilds in the flood regime 0 across all runs
(before: phase-race, 0–5 per 30s in-process bench); frame-build
p99 5.0ms / max 7.4ms flat over 60s; echo p99 43.6ms, max 57.3ms
(residual tail is event-loop/GC noise from the flood itself, bounded,
not growing with transcript size). Bench:
`dart run scripts/tui_typing_bench.dart --grow-tail` (in-process rebuild
counters; seeds the submit-echo lines so the flood grows the LAST line
like the shipped REPL). Contracts: the split-resume trio in
`test/cli/transcript_markdown_perf_test.dart`.

## Table rendering — adversarial TDD round (post-optimization)

The speedup initially exposed (and testing then pinned) a real streaming-table
correctness bug — the same class as the historical "tables fall apart while a
run streams" reports:

*Root cause.* The durable-commit boundary advanced past a STILL-OPEN table.
The frozen snapshot carries only fence state; buffered table rows live solely
in the parser buffer, so once the boundary crossed them those leading rows
were never re-consumed — later renders lost the header row or shifted cells,
and rebuilds ended pending with unreplayable state.

*Invariant now enforced* (`TranscriptMarkdown._commitTo`):

> The commit edge stops at the last CLEAN step — it NEVER advances into an
> open table span (`through = from + lastClean + 1`). Until the table closes,
> its whole span stays provisional: every flush re-renders exactly that span
> from the frozen state and replaces the previous frame wholesale (no ghosts,
> no stacking), which also keeps late-widening columns safe. Close drains the
> full rendered grid into durable caches exactly once.

Both resume and rebuild paths share one walker (`_walk` → `_commitTo` /
`_expose`), so the invariant cannot drift between them.

Contracts: `test/cli/transcript_table_render_test.dart` — stepped parity at
every prefix (including ending-mid-table), late column widening, CJK/emoji
display widths + border-alignment checks on s…

This is a large codebase. Let me step back and think about the ACTUAL symptom again, focusing on the strongest hint:

"Suspect: transcript commit offset (O(delta)) re-emitting already-committed lines when a service line (job settle, btw) is inserted between the live area and the previous commit."

The phrase "re-emitting already-committed lines" and the observed "answer re-written over the live area in two layouts" sounds like the TERMINAL VISUAL: content that belongs in the scrollback/history area got re-printed INSIDE the live area region. In alt-screen rendering, "the live area" = the bottom rows of the frame (busy row / composer / job rows). The answer text painted over those rows...

Actually wait. What about the physical screen-scroll behavior: when the frame grows taller than the terminal (frame rows > termHeight), `_cropToGlass` drops from the top. But BEFORE that guard existed... it exists.

Alternative: the CellRenderer's scroll-region fast path (CSI S/CSI T). Scenario: answer streams in → history grows → the frame's history window slides down (rows shift UP). The renderer detects a shift-up by k, emits `CSI kS` (scroll up), then repaints the k fresh rows at the bottom. If, instead, the content change is NOT a pure shift (e.g. a service row inserted in the live area changes the middle), and detection still picks a k within tolerance... then the "repaint" rows are only the mismatches — but a shift op PHYSICALLY scrolls the screen, pushing the top rows off — in alt screen, top rows are LOST, and the invariant check (static-edge) rejects... The static-edge check rejects when the EDGE row is identical AND non-blank.

Consider: transcript window with sticky chrome at row 0. New frame: history shifted up by k (fresh answer rows at the bottom of the window), sticky echo at row 0 IDENTICAL (the pinned user echo stays). Edge row 0 identical + non-blank → REJECT the scroll op → cell diff. OK.

But suppose row 0 changed slightly (spinner frame in the busy row? no that's lower). Or the top edge is a BLANK row (blank edge "scrolls without a visible trace, so it keeps the fast path"). Hmm — "A blank edge scrolls without a visible trace" — if the top row is blank padding, CSI S pushes it off, blank at bottom gets repainted. Fine.

Now consider shift DOWN (-k, CSI T): e.g. the job board row DISAPPEARS (job settles → row removed) → the composer/status move UP... that means content below the removed row shifts UP by 1 while history stays → mixed. Detection requires a GLOBAL shift (majority). With a 24-row screen, one removed row shifts ~8 rows up; majority fails → cell diff. OK.

Hmm, so the scroll fast path seems well-guarded (that's #761, and it's the vendored dart_tui 2.1.0).

blocks.text:
# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` / `--timer`/`--deadline` / `/timer` write one
  session clock, the per-turn context carries a `time-left:` line while
  armed, and one-shot system notices steer wrap-up at ~50%, T-3min
  (drain background jobs), and T-30s; absent deadline = byte-for-byte
  today's behavior.

- gh-1522: tag-sourced versions — the git tag is the single source of
  truth. The release-bot file bumps are retired: cutting a release = a
  tag + GitHub Release (zero commits to main, zero file mutations).
  Both pubspecs carry the fixed `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (CI guards
  hand-bumps), the publish job stamps the staged pubspec + generated
  changelog section from the tag (`scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`,
  staged version == tag guarded pre-upload), store builds stamp
  `--build-name/--build-number` from the derived tag version
  (`pubspec.lock` stops churning across releases), and
  `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from `git describe`.

- feat(usage): gh-1460 — the `fa-tokens:` segment-close line carries the
  session's model id, so every token row the factory publishes is
  attributable to a model and therefore priceable. The fold now captures
  each segment's LAST-SEEN model id (the model that served the final
  request, the same string settings/UI display — mid-session fallback
  take-overs attribute the segment to the model that actually finished it;
  zero-filled fallbacks never clobber a seen model) and the pinned line
  shape grows an OPTIONAL `"model":"<id>"` key after `"segment"` — omitted
  when no model was observed, so legacy lines parse unchanged and the
  pinned regex (`usageTokensLogPattern`, gh-1241 AC7) keeps matching both
  shapes. usage.json's schema is untouched (the model is rebuildable from
  the chain, I6); old consumers using tolerant JSON ignore the new key,
  and the repo's single strict consumer (the pinned constant) is updated
  in the same change.

- fix(test): gh-1460 rework — the `wrap_ansi_line_perf_test` growth-shape
  legs measure the doubling ratio with the MINIMUM over 9 runs instead of
  the median of 5 (CI run 38112524699, core shard 0/4: a scheduling pause
  inflated the doubled-size median — 12.09ms against a true ~7ms — and
  tripped the 3.2 bound at 3.65x on a genuinely linear wrap). Runner
  jitter only ever inflates a wall-clock sample, so the min converges on
  the true compute time; genuine superlinearity still trips the ratio
  (the gh-1496 quadratic candidates measure ~4x by min). The absolute-
  budget legs keep the median — their gh-1357 headroom already prices in
  jitter. A synthetic regression test pins the pause-proof property.

## 1.0.506

- fix(#1044): AIIN mobile/macOS add-provider — sign-in completes but the provider is never added (#1194)
- fix(ci): pass flutter-version explicitly — awf no longer defaults a toolchain (#1205)

## 1.0.507

- gh-1208 [BENCH] fix-git task image broken on CI runners — docker compose build fails in BOTH TBench-1 runs (unknown_agent_error, trial never starts) (#1218)
- gh-1206 WIP auto-save 2026-10-04T05-52-28 (#1216)
- gh-1209 [BENCH] usage fold skips failed trials — agent_timeout rows report 0/0 tokens though the session JSONL has full usage (#1123 follow-up) (#1215)

## 1.0.508

- fix(cli): gh-1459 — headless `fa -p` no longer orphans live background
  shell jobs. `_awaitHeadlessBackgroundJobs` drained only in-flight
  subagent jobs, so a run whose model was still waiting on a
  `bash background:true` command (gh-1440's full test suite) printed the
  detach summary and exited, killing the job with the container — the
  result it was explicitly waiting for never reached anyone. Live shell
  jobs now drain exactly like subagents: the settles ride the existing
  `_onShellJobSettled` fresh-turn path (steered into reaction runs the
  drain awaits, loop capped at 10 rounds), suppressed jobs
  (`suppressSettleNotification` — result already landed in-turn) are not
  awaited, and a settle landing outside a round still gets its reaction
  run awaited before exit. BOTH loops share ONE wall-clock ceiling, the
  new `headless:` config section (`shellJobDrainMs`, default 30 min,
  strict parse; `0` restores the detach-immediately behavior) — a
  never-settling watch-loop detaches with an observable
  `⏳ … drain ceiling … — detaching` line instead of hanging headless,
  and the detach summary stays the documented degradation, never the
  default path. The drain prints a `⏳ waiting: …` line (#1055 parity)
  naming what the run stays alive for. While it waits, the drain also
  steers interim liveness notices (gh-1459 ask #4): every
  `headless.shellJobQuietMs` (default 5 min; `0` = off) of a
  still-running awaited shell job, ONE compact system-notice
  (`job <id> running · <elapsed> elapsed · tail: …` plus the bash_job
  output/stop escape hatch) keeps the model able to wait, inspect, or
  kill instead of blocking blindly to the ceiling; a crossing the model
  probed itself (`bash_job status/output` bumps the entry's probe
  generation) is skipped, one steer budget per threshold, never a spam
  loop.
- feat(providers): issue #1398 — stall-recovery tuning becomes per-provider
  and data-driven. Registry entries (`customProviders:`, `models.custom:`,
  roles chain entries, `providersQueue:` entries) accept optional
  `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs` (strict positive-int parsing);
  resolution is **entry > the `providerTimeouts:` section > the 180 s/300 s
  defaults**, per field, and every seeded entry prints its effective values

The ticket says version 1.0.547 showed the bug, asks whether it's fixed in 1.0.565. Let me now write a quick reproduction attempt mentally and then actually examine the transcript sync logic for the "service line inserted" scenario.

The claim: "transcript commit offset (O(delta)) re-emitting already-committed lines when a service line (job settle, btw) is inserted between the live area and the previous commit."

Scenario in outputLines terms:
1. Answer streams: lines appended. Last line grows without newline. Commits track it.
2. A `[btw]` notice arrives → `sendOutput('[btw] ...', newline: true)` — appends '\n'... wait, actually the host appends text WITH newline. Let me check the exact append shape: `_appendOutput(lines, text, newline)`: splits text on '\n', merges first part into last line, adds the rest, and if newline=true adds ANOTHER empty line.

Actually wait — for the streaming answer, deltas arrive via `io.write(delta)` → `sendOutput(delta)` with newline=false. The trailing `io.write('\n')` at message end → sendOutput('\n') → parts = ['',''], first part merges ('' into last line), then adds '' → i.e. terminates the last line and opens a new empty line.

So during streaming, outputLines ends with a growing line. `_through` == src.length after each sync (committing the growing tail line!). Then next delta: src[_through-1] is a NEW longer string with the same prefix → `_rollbackGrownTail` rolls back one line and re-walks. Fine.

NOW: a service line (btw notice) lands BETWEEN answer deltas? The ticket: "Happens after a background bash job settles (row like sh-3-...) and [btw] notices about mail/scheduler." The btw notices and job-settle service lines arrive WHILE THE ANSWER IS STREAMING (the answer is the last thing; the notices arrive mid-stream or right at the end).

Order of events for the observed bug:
1. The final answer streams into the transcript (with a table inside → table layout).
2. Meanwhile, service lines (btw) get appended — they go AFTER the growing answer line (outputLines append). That's fine.
3. ...

Hmm, but where would "re-emitting already-committed lines" produce VISIBLE duplication? If TranscriptMarkdown served a stale view (e.g. published `_viewRows` built from OLD `_rows` + new tail WITHOUT the truncation), you'd get duplicated rows!

LOOK at `_expose` closely:

```dart
void _expose(_WalkResult r, List<String> src) {
  final tailStartStep = r.lastClean + 1;
  final tailLines = <String>[
    for (var step = tailStartStep; step < r.outsPerLine.length; step++)
      ...r.outsPerLine[step],
    ...r.trailing,
  ];
  if (tailLines.isEmpty) {
    _publishCleanViews();
    return;
  }
  ...
}
```

`tailLines` = outputs of steps AFTER the commit edge + trailing flush. This looks right.

And in `sync()`:

```dart
final r = _walk(src, from: _through);
_commitTo(r, src, from: _through);
_expose(r, src);
```

_commitTo appends `r.outsPerLine[step]` for step < upto where upto = lastClean+1. So committed steps [0, lastClean], tail steps (lastClean, ...). No overlap. OK.

BUT WAIT — `_rollbackGrownTail`: it rolls back ONE source line (`edge = _through - 1`) and truncates caches. Then `sync` continues:

```dart
if (!_resumable(src) && !_rollbackGrownTail(src)) { _rebuild(src); return _viewFormatted; }
if (src.length == _through) { return _viewFormatted; }  // nothing new
...
if (_tailThrottled(src)) { debugTailThrottled++; return _viewFormatted; }
...
final r = _walk(src, from: _through);
_commitTo(r, src, from: _through);
_expose(r, src);
```

After a successful rollback: _through = edge = old _through - 1. src.length is >= _through. If src.length == _through (rollback of the last line but no new lines?) — e.g. the line SHRANK? No: faithful growth means longer.

Hmm OK. Now the table case! The commit edge NEVER advances into an open table span. Consider the answer contains a TABLE (markdown table), and the table is OPEN at the end of the streamed-so-far content (the last rows of the table have arrived but the table hasn't been closed by a blank line / non-table line yet). Then `lastClean` points BEFORE the table start; `upto` stops there. The WHOLE TABLE SPAN is provisional: on every flush it's re-walked from `from = _through` — i.e. `_walk(src, from: _through)` where _through is before the table lines; the walk RE-consumes all the table lines and re-renders them. `_expose` then publishes `_viewRows = [..._rows, ...tailRows]` — a fresh copy with the provisional tail. Still no duplication: `_rows` (durable) has nothing after the boundary.

Hmm, so where's the bug?!

Let me look at the case where `lastClean == -1` and `upto <= 0` → `_commitTo` returns early without doing anything. Then `_expose` with tailStartStep = 0 → tailLines = ALL steps' outputs + trailing. Views = _rows (durable, up to boundary) + tail. Still fine.

OK let me now go look at the OTHER consumer of the wrap cache — `_writeStickyEcho` and `_echoEndRow`, plus `stickyIndex`/`stickyLines` — because "the answer rendered 3-4 times... first as a table, then as flowing text" could ALSO be: the sticky echo pinned... no, sticky is the user echo.

WAIT. Let me re-read the ticket: "The answer is re-written over the live area in two layouts: first as a table, then as flowing text with lines glued together (...гарде2. Issue ...)".

What if this is about the **frame diff** in the CELL renderer: rows are only repainted when changed. If the frame content JUMPS (e.g. transcript window content changed completely due to a full rebuild serving DIFFERENT rows), the diff repaints each changed row IN PLACE. If the model produced a frame where the same answer is painted in the history window AND ALSO duplicated rows exist in outputLines... the "two layouts" strongly suggest TWO COPIES of the answer in the FRAME CONTENT itself: one formatted as a table, one raw/glued.

"Lines glued together" — `...гарде2. Issue ...` — this looks like two lines WITHOUT the newline: "гарде" + "2. Issue". When would newlines be lost? If the answer text was re-emitted via a path that STRIPS newlines... e.g. writing text via `io.write` where '\n' separators were replaced...

OR — soft-wrapping! When a long line soft-wraps at the terminal width, the continuation rows flow like glued text. If the answer was committed to the transcript as ONE GIANT LINE (no newlines) it would render as flowing glued text (wrapped at width). So the two layouts:
1. Table layout: the answer WITH structure (markdown source lines, table parsed).
2. Flowing glued text: the same answer content re-appended as ONE LONG LINE (newlines lost!).

Where would the answer get re-emitted with newlines lost?? `io.write(delta)` — deltas... `io.write(text)` where text = the FULL message...

AH WAIT. I bet I know! Look at `_flushAssistantStreamAtEnd` — for `_useTui` it does `io.write('\n')` and resets. But what about a RETRY path — when a provider stream FAILS mid-answer and is retried (silent_stream_policy / stall recovery, ApiKeyRing takeover, provider fallback chains!). On a mid-stream failure + retry, does the TUI transcript get RESET/rewound before the retry re-streams the answer? If NOT, the answer would be duplicated: partial stream + full re-stream. "rendered 3-4 times" = several retries (silent_stream_policy: codex-style backoff 5→60s, rotation after 2nd stall, smol takeover after 3rd — up to 3-4 attempts!). AND: "happens after a background bash job settles and [btw] notices" — the retry/steer flow!

Hmm wait, but stalls... The user's report: version 1.0.547, happens after background bash job settles + btw notices. If each retry re-streamed the whole answer, the transcript would hold 3-4 copies (and the session file would too — but the session file holds ONE record... hmm, that contradicts).

Hold on — "The session file holds a single record, so the duplication is in rendering only." So the agent produced ONE assistant message record. The TUI transcript shows it 3-4 times…
